stem:
Meera visits a geology exhibition in Jaipur with her class. She reads three display labels:

1. Granite contains the minerals quartz, feldspar and mica, which can be seen as separate grains in the rock.
2. Calcite is a mineral with the fixed composition CaCO₃ (calcium carbonate).
3. A sample of native gold from a mine contains only gold atoms.

Meera must classify each sample as a mixture, a compound, or a pure element. Which row of the table is correct?

options.text: Granite – compound; calcite – mixture; native gold – pure element
Granite – mixture; calcite – compound; native gold – pure element
Granite – mixture; calcite – compound; native gold – mixture
Granite – mixture; calcite – pure element; native gold – compound

teacher.key_rationale: Granite contains several visibly different minerals physically combined, so it is a mixture. Calcite has a fixed chemical composition (CaCO₃) of more than one element chemically combined, so it is a compound. Native gold contains only one kind of atom, so it is a pure element. Row B matches all three classifications.
